subject: economics
title: Unemployment and Inflation
welcome_lead: Two big macro problems - and how to spot each type.
meta_desc: A-Level Macroeconomics: types of unemployment and inflation.
final_note: Policy must match the cause - demand-side or supply-side.

concepts.def: Mismatch between skills and jobs available.
Caused by downturns in aggregate demand.
Consumer Prices Index - basket of consumer goods.
Retail Prices Index - older UK measure, includes housing.

walkthroughs.body_html: Frictional unemployment is benign; structural needs retraining; cyclical needs demand stimulus. Mistaking the type wastes policy effort.
CPI uses a basket of consumer goods. RPI includes housing costs and tends to be higher. Both miss housing price inflation in the same way.
Demand-pull inflation comes from excess AD; cost-push inflation from rising input costs (oil, wages). The response differs - tighten policy vs supply-side reforms.

Structural unemployment is unemployment caused by a recession.

Unemployment caused by a mismatch between workers' skills/location and available jobs — often due to long-term economic change like deindustrialisation.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between CPI and RPI as inflation measures?
options: The Phillips curve shows the link between phone use and unemployment.
CPI and RPI always give the same inflation figure.
CPI measures consumer prices and RPI measures retail prices — that's the only difference.

Both measure price changes via a basket of goods, but RPI includes housing costs (mortgage interest) and uses an arithmetic mean; CPI excludes housing costs and uses a geometric mean — CPI is the official UK target measure.

mcqs.q: What did the original Phillips curve suggest, and how has thinking changed?
options: The original Phillips curve suggested a stable inverse relationship between unemployment and inflation. Friedman and the 1970s stagflation experience added expectations — the long-run Phillips curve is vertical at the natural rate of unemployment.
Structural unemployment is when people are too lazy to work.
The Phillips curve shows the link between phone use and unemployment.
The Phillips curve still proves you can always reduce unemployment by allowing more inflation.
